docs.title: Ella SMSC
docs.text: Ella SMSC lets private cellular network subscribers send and receive SMS messages. It is an SMS Service Center (SMSC) that integrates with 4G and 5G core networks.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• SMS over 4G and 5G: phones send and receive SMS through the MME or SMSF of the core, over SGd, with routing from the HSS over S6c.
  • SMS over IP: phones registered with an IP-SM-GW, such as Ella IMS's, send and receive SMS through it.
  • Store and forward: messages wait while a phone is unreachable, are retried, and go out as soon as the HSS says it is back, within their validity period.
  • 3GPP compliant: status reports, replace short message and reject duplicates, per TS 23.040 and TS 29.338.
  • Application messages: send text from the web UI or the HTTP API, from a number or a name such as EllaSMSC, and binary messages such as SIM OTA updates from the HTTP API.
  • Delivery visibility: every routing lookup and delivery attempt is recorded, with why it failed.
  • Secure: users with roles, API tokens, HTTPS, and audited reads of message content.
  • Easy to operate: a single binary with an embedded database and configurable retention, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics. Install with snap, Docker or Kubernetes.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
These explanations provide context on how Ella SMSC works.

  • Architecture
  • Security

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: A Short Message Service Centre (SMSC) stores the short messages phones send, and forwards them to their recipients. Ella SMSC is a single process, with one SQLite database, one UI, one API and, when configured, an SMPP listener.

docs.title: Where Ella SMSC sits
docs.text:
Ella SMSC has no radio access and stores no subscribers. It relies on the core network, over Diameter:

  • The HSS, over S6c, says where a recipient is served, and alerts the SMSC when an unreachable recipient is back.
  • The MME or SMSF, over SGd, carries messages between the phones and the SMSC, in NAS signalling.
  • An IP-SM-GW, over SGd, carries them for phones registered for SMS over IP.

Ella Core provides the HSS, the MME and the SMSF. For how it works with an SMSC, see Ella Core's SMS Integration.

Ella SMSC's Diameter host and realm derive from the operator's MCC and MNC: smsc.node.epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org in the realm epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org. Its peers connect to it, and it asks the HSSs of that realm for routing.

docs.title: Reaching other networks
docs.text:
A subscriber roaming on another network is served by a visited MME or SMSF that never connects to Ella SMSC. Ella SMSC reaches it through a Diameter agent it connects to, such as the edge agent of the operator or of an IPX provider. An HSS behind a DRA is reached the same way.

Each agent has routes: the realms it reaches. A default route takes every other realm, except Ella SMSC's own, so a home MME that is briefly disconnected is retried rather than sent out to the IPX. An agent is asked only for the requests of its routes: an HSS added as an agent needs an S6c route to Ella SMSC's realm.

When an agent fails with a short message in flight, Ella SMSC sends it through the next one, and the subscriber may receive it twice.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
A phone's message reaches Ella SMSC when the SMSC number on its SIM card is Ella SMSC's service centre address. The MME, SMSF or IP-SM-GW gives the phone's MSISDN, which is the sender. Ella SMSC converts the recipient to an international number with the operator's numbering plan, stores the message, and acknowledges it.

Applications send messages to phones with the Messages API, or over SMPP.

docs.title: Delivering
docs.text:
For each message, Ella SMSC asks the HSS for the serving nodes of the recipient, then tries them in turn until one takes the message. Messages to a phone go one at a time, in order. When more wait, the serving node that took one takes the next, without another routing lookup.

Each lookup and delivery is recorded as an attempt, shown in the UI and the API.

docs.title: When a phone is unreachable
docs.text:
When no serving node takes a message, Ella SMSC makes sure the HSS records that a message waits. The message and the recipient's other messages wait for a retry, after the retry intervals. When the phone can receive messages again, the HSS alerts Ella SMSC, which delivers them right away.

A message ends:

  • delivered, when a serving node takes it;
  • failed, when the recipient is unknown, not allowed SMS, or has no serving node that supports SGd, when the SIM refuses a (U)SIM data download message, or when an attempt fails and the message is single-shot or retries are off;
  • expired, when its validity period ends first;
  • replaced, when a later message from the same sender replaces it. A message from the Messages API or an ESME is replaced only by one from the same user or ESME.

docs.title: Status reports
docs.text: When a phone asks for status reports, Ella SMSC returns one to it when the message ends. It delivers the report as it does a message.

docs.title: ESMEs over SMPP
docs.text:
Platforms built for SMSCs, such as OTA platforms, connect as External Short Message Entities (ESMEs), over SMPP 3.4:

OTA platform (ESME) ──SMPP over TCP or TLS, 2775──▶ SMPP listener ──▶ submission ──▶ database ──▶ delivery ──▶ HSS, MME, SMSF
        ▲                                                                                       │
        └──────────────── deliver_sm: receipts, SIM answers ◀── notifications ◀─────────────────┘
  • The SMPP listener accepts the ESMEs' connections, checks each bind against the ESME accounts, and keeps the sessions. An ESME account acts as a user: the messages it submits are that user's, and the user's role decides what it may do.
  • Submission. Each submit_sm becomes one short message, through the same path as the Messages API, so the same parameters give the same message. Ella SMSC answers once the message is stored, then delivers it as any other.
  • Notifications. When a message from an ESME ends, Ella SMSC queues the delivery receipt and the SIM's answer that the ESME asked for. It sends them as deliver_sm to a receiving session of that ESME, the answer first, and keeps them until the ESME acknowledges them, binds again, or they expire. They survive a restart.

See the SMPP reference.

docs.title: Binary messages
docs.text: Applications can send binary messages, such as the (U)SIM data download messages that an OTA platform sends to update SIM cards: the phone passes them to the SIM instead of showing them. Ella SMSC delivers their parameters and user data unchanged, and keeps the phone's answer to each delivery attempt, which can carry the SIM's response.

docs.title: Users and roles
docs.text:
Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role: Admin, Read Only, Network Manager or Submitter. The role decides what the user can see and do, from reading settings to managing other users. See Roles.

The first user, an Admin, is created when Ella SMSC is initialized. Admins create the others.

Ella SMSC limits login attempts, from each address and for each account, to slow down password guessing.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
Applications, such as an OTA platform, use an API token rather than a password. A token belongs to a user and has that user's role, but it cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users. Tokens can expire, and an Admin or the token's user can delete one at any time.

Give each application its own Submitter user: it can send messages, and read only the messages it sent.

docs.title: ESMEs
docs.text:
An ESME, such as an OTA platform, binds to the SMPP listener with a system_id and a password. SMPP 3.4 limits that password to 8 characters, so Ella SMSC adds other checks:

  • Each ESME acts as a user, whose role decides whether it may submit or receive.
  • An ESME binds only from the networks in its allow-list. An empty list allows no address.
  • Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes. A password the SMSC generates has 8 random letters and digits.
  • Binds are limited from each address, and wrong passwords for each ESME. Every refused bind gets the same answer, so a client cannot tell which check failed.
  • Only an Admin, logged in rather than with an API token, creates, changes or deletes ESMEs.

SMPP 3.4 has no encryption: the password and the messages cross the network in clear. TLS, with smpp.tls, is a common convention outside SMPP 3.4, which the ESME must support. Use plain TCP only over a private link, such as an IPsec VPN, or in a lab.

The allow-list checks the address of the TCP connection. Terminate TLS in Ella SMSC itself, not in a proxy or load balancer, which would hide the ESME's address. On Kubernetes, the Service keeps it with externalTrafficPolicy: Local.

docs.title: Message content
docs.text: Messages carry personal content. Reading it is a permission of its own: a Read Only user sees that messages were sent and delivered, but not what they say. Every read of the content is recorded in an audit event, with who read it and from where.

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text: Ella SMSC serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in api.tls (see the configuration file). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

docs.title: Diameter peers
docs.text:
Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that connects and supports S6c or SGd, and its Diameter connections are not encrypted. Keep its Diameter address on a network that only the core network can reach.

Through an edge agent, other networks can send short messages to Ella SMSC, which does not filter them by realm. Have the edge agent accept only the operator's roaming partners.

docs.title: Back Up and Restore
docs.text:
Ella SMSC keeps all its data, messages, users and settings, in one database file: db.path in the configuration file. The commands below use the snap's path, /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db.

The backup holds message content and user accounts. Store and transfer it encrypted.

docs.title: Back up
docs.text:
1. Stop Ella SMSC:

    sudo snap stop ella-smsc.smscd

  2. Copy the database:

    sudo cp /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db smsc-backup.db

  3. Start Ella SMSC:

    sudo snap start ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. Stop Ella SMSC:

    sudo snap stop ella-smsc.smscd

  2. Replace the database with the backup, and remove the files that go with the old one:

    sudo cp smsc-backup.db /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db
sudo rm -f /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db-wal /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db-shm

  3. Start Ella SMSC:

    sudo snap start ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: Connect through Diameter Agents
docs.text: This guide connects Ella SMSC to an edge agent (DEA), to deliver short messages to roaming subscribers, and to a DRA in front of the HSS.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: integrated with its core, as in Integrate with a Third-Party Core.
  • A user with the Network Manager or Admin role.
  • The agents: their Diameter hosts and SCTP addresses. Each has Ella SMSC's host, realm and Diameter address as a peer.
  • The visited networks: support SMS in MME (SGd), or an SMSF with a Diameter host and realm.

The examples use these values:

Value Role dea1.ipx.example.net, 192.0.2.10, 198.51.100.10 Edge agent dra1.example.net, 10.3.0.20 DRA in front of the HSS epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org Ella SMSC's realm

docs.title: 1. Add the edge agent
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter and click Add Peer:

  • Host: dea1.ipx.example.net
  • Addresses: 192.0.2.10, 198.51.100.10, every SCTP address of the agent.
  • Port: 3868

Click Add Route, and keep Application set to SGd and Destination to Default. Click Add.

To add a backup agent, repeat with its host and addresses, and set the route's Priority to 1.

docs.title: 2. Add the DRA
docs.text:
Skip this step if the HSS connects to Ella SMSC.

Click Add Peer:

  • Host: dra1.example.net
  • Addresses: 10.3.0.20
  • Port: 3868

Click Add Route, and set:

  • Application: S6c
  • Destination: Realm
  • Realm: epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org

Click Add.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
On the Diameter page, under Configured Peers:

  • Each agent shows open. Hover over another state to see why.
  • The DRA shows HSS set to yes.

Send a short message to a roaming subscriber. On the Messages page, it shows delivered.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Choose one of the installation methods below.

Snap (Recommended)SourceDockerKubernetes

Install the Ella SMSC snap:

sudo snap install ella-smsc

Configure Ella SMSC:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml

Start Ella SMSC:

sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd

Install the required dependencies:

sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc

Clone the Ella SMSC repository:

git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc.git
cd smsc

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella SMSC:

go build -o smsc -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/smsc/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/smsc

Configure Ella SMSC:

vim smsc.yaml

Start Ella SMSC:

./smsc --config smsc.yaml

Create a new directory:

mkdir ella-smsc
cd ella-smsc

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_smsc_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/smsc.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5010
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.7

services:
  ella-smsc:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-smsc:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_smsc_config
        target: /smsc.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/smsc --config /smsc.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - ella-smsc-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-smsc-data:

Set diameter.address to an address of the host that the core can reach.

Start the Ella SMSC container:

docker compose up -d

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the Multus CNI installed, and the sctp kernel module loaded on its nodes.

Download the Ella SMSC manifests:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc.git

Edit smsc/k8s/smsc-diameter-nad.yaml to set master to the host interface that connects to your core, and set the Diameter address. Use the same address for diameter.address in smsc/k8s/smsc-configmap.yaml.

Deploy Ella SMSC:

kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl apply -k smsc/k8s

Ella SMSC's UI and API are on the ella-smsc NodePort Service.

To enable SMPP, uncomment the smpp block in smsc/k8s/smsc-configmap.yaml, or smsc/k8s/pod-network/smsc-configmap.yaml. SMPP is on the pod network, port 2775 of the ella-smsc Service, in both variants. The Service has externalTrafficPolicy: Local, so the SMSC sees the ESMEs' own addresses, which their allowed networks are checked against. Terminate TLS in the SMSC pod, with smpp.tls and a Secret mounted in the pod: a load balancer, sidecar or ingress that terminates TLS hides the client address.

Ella SMSC's UI and API are at http://<host-ip>:5010. Open the UI and create the first user.

With an smpp block in the configuration file, Ella SMSC listens for SMPP 3.4 ESMEs, such as OTA platforms, on port 2775. See SMPP.

See the configuration reference for all options.

docs.title: Integrate with Ella Core
docs.text: This guide connects Ella SMSC to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS (S6c) and the MME or SMSF (SGd).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: installed and started, as in Install.

The examples use these values:

Value Role 10.3.0.7 Ella SMSC's Diameter address 001 / 01 Ella Core's MCC and MNC +15550000000 Ella SMSC's service centre address +15550001111 Ella Core's SMS number

docs.title: 1. Set the Diameter address
docs.text:
In smsc.yaml, set the address Ella Core reaches Ella SMSC on, and restart Ella SMSC:

diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7

docs.title: 2. Set the operator
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the Operator page:

  • Click the edit icon next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), enter Ella Core's MCC and MNC, e.g. 001 / 01, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Service Centre Address, enter +15550000000, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Numbering, enter your country code and prefixes, and click Update.

Go to the Diameter page and note the Host, e.g. smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org.

docs.title: 3. Add Ella SMSC to Ella Core
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to Operator and scroll to the SMS section:

  • Check that SMS Number is set, e.g. +15550001111, Ella Core's default.
  • Click Add Service Center, enter:
    • Address: 10.3.0.7
    • Numbers: +15550000000
    • Diameter Identity: the Host of step 2.
  • Click Add.

The service center shows Connected.

docs.title: 4. Give subscribers an MSISDN
docs.text: In the Ella Core UI, for each subscriber that sends or receives SMS, go to Subscribers, open the subscriber, click the edit icon next to MSISDN, enter its E.164 number, e.g. +15551230001, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Set the SMSC number on the SIM cards
docs.text: On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to +15550000000.

docs.title: 6. Verify
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers, Ella Core shows open, with HSS set to yes.

Send an SMS between two phones. On the Messages page, it shows delivered.

docs.title: Integrate with Ella IMS
docs.text: This guide lets Ella SMSC deliver SMS to phones registered for SMS over IP with Ella IMS's IP-SM-GW. Phones send SMS over IP to Ella SMSC the same way.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: connected to Ella Core, as in Integrate with Ella Core.
  • Ella IMS: connected to Ella Core, as in Ella IMS's Integrate with Ella Core.

The examples use 10.3.0.7 as Ella SMSC's Diameter address and +15550000000 as its service centre address.

docs.title: 1. Enable SMS over IP in Ella IMS
docs.text:
Follow Ella IMS's Enable SMS over IP guide. When you add the SMSC, enter:

  • Address: 10.3.0.7
  • Roles: SGd only
  • Service Centres: 15550000000
  • Transport: SCTP
  • Host: the Host of Ella SMSC's Diameter page, e.g. smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org

docs.title: 2. Verify
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers, Ella IMS shows open, with Applications set to SGd and HSS set to no.

Send an SMS to a phone registered for SMS over IP. On the Messages page, click the message: its delivery attempt went to Ella IMS's host, marked (IP-SM-GW).

docs.title: Integrate with a Third-Party Core
docs.text: This guide connects Ella SMSC to a 4G or 5G core other than Ella Core, through its HSS (S6c) and its MMEs or SMSFs (SGd).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: installed and started, as in Install.
  • HSS: supports S6c, in the realm epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org of the core's PLMN.
  • MME or SMSF: supports SGd, and gives the MSISDN of the phone in each short message it forwards. The HSS names it, in its routing answers, by the Diameter identity it connects to Ella SMSC with.

The examples use 10.3.0.7 as Ella SMSC's Diameter address, 001 / 01 as the core's MCC and MNC, and +15550000000 as Ella SMSC's service centre address.

docs.title: 1. Set the Diameter address
docs.text:
In smsc.yaml, set the address the core reaches Ella SMSC on, and restart Ella SMSC:

diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7

docs.title: 2. Set the operator
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the Operator page:

  • Click the edit icon next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), enter the core's MCC and MNC, e.g. 001 / 01, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Service Centre Address, enter +15550000000, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Numbering, enter your country code and prefixes, and click Update.

The Diameter page shows Ella SMSC's Host and Realm, e.g. smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org and epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org.

docs.title: 3. Add Ella SMSC to the core
docs.text:
In the HSS, and in each MME or SMSF, add Ella SMSC as a Diameter peer:

  • Address: 10.3.0.7
  • Port: 3868
  • Transport: SCTP
  • Host and Realm: those of step 2.
  • Application: S6c in the HSS, SGd in the MME or SMSF.

In each MME or SMSF, route the short messages of service centre address +15550000000 to Ella SMSC.

docs.title: 4. Provision the subscribers
docs.text: In the HSS, give each subscriber that sends or receives SMS an MSISDN. On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to +15550000000.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers:

  • The HSS shows open, with HSS set to yes. If it shows no, its realm differs from Ella SMSC's, or it does not support S6c.
  • Each MME or SMSF shows open, with SGd in Applications.

Send an SMS between two phones. On the Messages page, it shows delivered.

See Connectivity and 3GPP Compliance for the interfaces Ella SMSC supports.

docs.title: Send Messages from an Application
docs.text: This guide gives an application, such as an OTA platform, an API token to send messages with.

docs.title: 1. Create a user for the application
docs.text:
In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:

  • Email: an address for the application, such as ota@example.com
  • Password: any password of at least 8 characters
  • Role: Submitter

Click Create.

docs.title: 2. Create an API token
docs.text:
Open the user, and in API Tokens, click Create Token. Name it after the application, check No expiry, and click Create.

Copy the token. It is not shown again.

docs.title: 3. Configure the application
docs.text:
Send a message with the token:

curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from": "+15550001000", "to": "+15551230002", "text": "hello"}'

See the Messages API.

docs.title: Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over SMPP
Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over SMPP
docs.text: This guide connects an OTA platform to Ella SMSC over SMPP 3.4 with TLS, sends a secured packet to a SIM with submit_sm, and receives the SIM's answer and a delivery receipt as deliver_sm.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: installed, as in Install.
  • A TLS certificate for the SMSC, smpp.pem, with its chain, and its private key, smpp.key, in PEM.
  • A user with the Admin role, logged in to the UI.
  • The OTA platform's network: the IP prefix it connects from, such as 10.1.0.0/24.
  • The secured packet, at most 140 octets with its user data header.

The examples use 15550001000 as the source and 15551230002 as the MSISDN of the SIM.

docs.title: 1. Enable the SMPP listener
docs.text:
Copy the certificate and key:

sudo cp smpp.pem smpp.key /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/
sudo chmod 600 /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.key

In /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml, add:

smpp:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 2775
  tls:
    cert: /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.pem
    key: /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.key

Restart Ella SMSC:

sudo snap restart ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: 2. Create a user for the OTA platform
docs.text:
In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:

  • Email: ota@example.com
  • Password: any password of at least 8 characters
  • Role: Submitter

Click Create.

docs.title: 3. Add the ESME
docs.text:
Go to SMPP and click Add ESME. Set:

  • System ID: ota
  • User: ota@example.com
  • Password: empty, to generate one
  • Allowed networks: 10.1.0.0/24

Click Add. Copy the generated password from the ESME Password dialog. It is not shown again.

docs.title: 4. Bind the OTA platform
docs.text:
Configure the OTA platform to bind as a transceiver, with:

Setting Value Host, port <host-ip>, 2775, over TLS system_id ota password The generated password interface_version 0x34

On the SMPP page, the Sessions of ota show Transceiver from the platform's address.

docs.title: 5. Submit the packet
docs.text:
Send a submit_sm with:

Field Value source_addr_ton, source_addr_npi, source_addr 1, 1, 15550001000 dest_addr_ton, dest_addr_npi, destination_addr 1, 1, 15551230002 esm_class 0x40, UDHI protocol_id 0x7F, (U)SIM data download data_coding 0xF6, 8-bit data, message class 2 registered_delivery 0x09: the SIM's answer and a delivery receipt short_message The packet's user data header, then the packet: 027000…

submit_sm_resp gives the message_id.

docs.title: 6. Receive the SIM's answer
docs.text:
The SMSC sends a deliver_sm with esm_class 0x50 and receipted_message_id set to the message_id. Its short_message is the SIM's Response Packet, 027100….

Answer it with deliver_sm_resp ESME_ROK.

docs.title: 7. Receive the delivery receipt
docs.text:
The SMSC sends a deliver_sm with esm_class 0x04 and receipted_message_id set to the message_id. Its short_message is the receipt:

id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:

Answer it with deliver_sm_resp ESME_ROK.

See the SMPP reference for every field, outcome and refusal.

docs.title: Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over the API
Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over the API
docs.text: This guide sends a secured packet that an OTA platform built to a SIM, over the HTTP API, and reads the SIM's answer.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An API token of a Submitter user, as in Send Messages from an Application.
  • The secured packet, at most 140 octets with its user data header, in hexadecimal.

docs.title: 1. Send the packet
docs.text:
Send the packet as a binary message, with:

  • protocol_identifier: 127, (U)SIM data download
  • data_coding_scheme: 246, 8-bit data, message class 2
  • user_data_header: the packet's user data header, such as 027000
  • user_data: the packet after its header
curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "from": "+15550001000",
        "to": "+15551230002",
        "binary": {
          "protocol_identifier": 127,
          "data_coding_scheme": 246,
          "user_data_header": "027000",
          "user_data": "<packet>"
        }
      }'

Note the id of the message in the response.

docs.title: 2. Wait for the delivery
docs.text:
Get the message until its status is no longer pending:

curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."

docs.title: 3. Read the SIM's answer
docs.text:
Get the content of the message:

curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages/<id>/content \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."

The SIM's answer is the user_data of the last item of deliver_reports. See Get the Content of a Message.

docs.text:
This section provides detailed reference material for Ella SMSC, from configuration options to complete API documentation.

docs.title: 3GPP Compliance
docs.text:
Ella SMSC implements the 3GPP SMSC of TS 23.040, with the S6c and SGd Diameter interfaces of TS 29.338.

Note

Open an issue if you notice a 3GPP-compliance gap or require a new capability for a production deployment.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text: Interface Peer Transport S6c HSS Diameter over SCTP SGd MME, SGSN, SMSF, IP-SM-GW Diameter over SCTP

docs.title: SGd (TS 29.338)
docs.text:
• MO-Forward-Short-Message, received: a phone's short message, from its MME, SMSF or IP-SM-GW.
  • MT-Forward-Short-Message, sent: a short message or a status report, to the phone's MME, SGSN, IP-SM-GW, or SMSF for 3GPP or non-3GPP access.

docs.title: S6c (TS 29.338)
docs.text:
• Send-Routing-Info-for-SM, sent: the serving nodes of the recipient, for a short message or a status report.
  • Report-SM-Delivery-Status, sent: the outcome of a delivery, which sets or clears the HSS's message waiting data.
  • Alert-Service-Centre, received: the recipient, or the Alert MSISDN of its subscription, can be reached again.

docs.title: Diameter routing (RFC 6733, GSMA IR.88)
docs.text:
• Static peers. Over SCTP, multi-homed.
  • Realm routing. Per realm and application, with a default route, and Destination-Host kept.
  • Failover. By priority, with load sharing, and the T flag on retransmission.

docs.title: Short messages (TS 23.040)
docs.text:
• TPDUs. SMS-SUBMIT received; SMS-DELIVER and SMS-STATUS-REPORT sent; SMS-SUBMIT-REPORT with the TP-Failure-Cause of a refused SMS-SUBMIT.
  • Store and forward. Messages to a phone are delivered in order, one at a time, and announce the next with TP-More-Messages-to-Send.
  • Validity period. Relative, absolute and enhanced formats, including single-shot messages.
  • Status reports. On the delivery, failure, expiry or replacement of a message whose sender set TP-Status-Report-Request.
  • Reject duplicates. TP-Reject-Duplicates.
  • Replace short message. Replace types 1 to 7 of TP-Protocol-Identifier, from phones, the API and SMPP. A message from the API or SMPP replaces only one of the same user or ESME.
  • Binary messages from the API. TP-Protocol-Identifier, TP-Data-Coding-Scheme, TP-User-Data-Header and TP-User-Data delivered unchanged, including (U)SIM data download.
  • SMS-DELIVER-REPORT. Kept from each delivery: in the SM-RP-UI of a successful MT-Forward-Short-Message answer, and in the SM-Diagnostic-Info of an SM Delivery Failure.
  • (U)SIM data download error. A message whose SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has the TP-Failure-Cause usim_data_download_error fails without another attempt.
  • SC time stamps. Distinct for the messages to a phone.
  • Numbering. International, national and unknown types of number, converted to international with the operator's numbering plan.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• SMS-COMMAND. Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause command_unsupported.
  • Telematic interworking. Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause telematic_interworking_not_supported.
  • Device triggering from phones. Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause unspecified_tp_pid_error.
  • SMS-MI-Correlation-ID. A short message that carries one is refused with DIAMETER_ERROR_FACILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.
  • Diameter over TCP.
  • Delivery to an MSC-Number.
  • Destination-Host in Report-SM-Delivery-Status.
  • MAP over SS7.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Ella SMSC is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella SMSC with the --config flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected. Changes take effect on restart.

The operator and delivery settings are not in this file: they are in the database, and set with the UI or the API.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• logging (object, optional): The logging configuration.
    • level (string, optional): The log level: debug, info, warn, or error. Default info.
  • db (object): The database configuration.
    • path (string): The path to the SQLite database file. Created if absent.
  • api (object): The HTTP API and UI.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 5010.
    • tls (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
    • drain_delay (duration, optional): How long Ella SMSC keeps serving after it is told to stop, with GET /api/v1/readyz failing. For example 5s. Default 0s.
  • diameter (object): Diameter, to the HSS, MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs.
    • name (string): The network interface to listen on, on all its addresses, advertised to peers. Either name or address must be set.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on, advertised to peers. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::. Either name or address must be set.
    • port (int, optional): The SCTP port to listen on. Default 3868.
  • smpp (object, optional): The SMPP 3.4 listener for ESMEs, such as OTA platforms. Without it, Ella SMSC does not listen for SMPP. The ESME accounts are in the database, managed with the API.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 2775. Not the API's port.
    • tls (object, optional): Wrap each connection in TLS, 1.2 or later, from its first octet. SMPP 3.4 has no TLS: this is a common convention, which the ESME must support. Default: plain TCP, for a private link or a lab only.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  • telemetry (object, optional): The traces.
    • enabled (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default false.
    • otlp_endpoint (string): The host:port of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when enabled is true.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: smsc.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5010
diameter:
  address: 127.0.0.1
  port: 3868
smpp:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 2775
  tls:
    cert: /etc/smsc/smpp.pem
    key: /etc/smsc/smpp.key
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp_endpoint: localhost:4317

With the snap, the configuration file is /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml.

docs.title: Connectivity
docs.text:
Interface Peer Transport Address Port API and UI Operators, applications, Prometheus TCP api.address api.port (5010) Diameter: S6c HSS SCTP diameter.address, or the addresses of diameter.name diameter.port (3868) Diameter: SGd MME, SMSF, IP-SM-GW SCTP diameter.address, or the addresses of diameter.name diameter.port (3868) Diameter: S6c and SGd, outbound Configured peers: DEA, DRA SCTP The peer's addresses The peer's port (3868) SMPP 3.4 ESMEs, such as OTA platforms TCP, or TLS with smpp.tls smpp.address smpp.port (2775)

Defaults are in parentheses. SMPP listens only when the configuration file has an smpp block.

Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that supports S6c or SGd. It connects to the configured peers, and reconnects after 1 to 30 seconds.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Ella SMSC supports four observability pillars: Metrics, Logs, Traces, and Profiles.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Ella SMSC exposes Prometheus metrics at GET /api/v1/metrics.

Metric Type Description ellasmsc_build_info Gauge Always 1. The version and revision of the running build are in its labels. ellasmsc_messages_received_total Counter Short messages received, one per part, by origin (mobile, api, smpp) and result (accepted, rejected, error). One per submit_sm for smpp. ellasmsc_messages_completed_total Counter Short messages and status reports that reached a final status, by type (message, status_report) and status (delivered, failed, expired, and replaced for a message). ellasmsc_messages_purged_total Counter Short messages deleted once their retention passed, with their status reports and delivery attempts. ellasmsc_messages_pending Gauge Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type and state: due, to be delivered now or being delivered; waiting, for a retry or for the phone to be reachable. ellasmsc_message_delivery_duration_seconds Histogram Time from submission to delivery of the short messages delivered, the time the phone was unreachable included. ellasmsc_hss_peers Gauge Open peers that serve S6c in the operator's realm: HSSs, or agents in front of them. At 0, messages to phones wait. ellasmsc_peer_requests_total Counter Requests to the HSS and to the MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs, by interface (s6c, sgd) and result (success, failure, absent_user, error, timeout). ellasmsc_peer_request_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of requests to the HSS and to the MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs, by interface. ellasmsc_smpp_sessions Gauge Bound SMPP sessions, by bind type (transmitter, receiver, transceiver). ellasmsc_smpp_binds_total Counter SMPP bind attempts, by result (accepted, rejected). ellasmsc_smpp_notifications_pending Gauge Delivery receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to an ESME and not expired, by type (receipt, sim_answer). A rise means no receiver of the ESME is bound, or it does not acknowledge them. ellasmsc_smpp_notifications_sent_total Counter Delivery receipts and SIM answers that reached a final outcome, by type and result (acknowledged, rejected, expired, no_user_data). ellasmsc_smpp_submit_duration_seconds Histogram Time from a submit_sm read to its submit_sm_resp written. ellasmsc_database_query_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of database calls, the wait for the connection included. ellasmsc_database_query_errors_total Counter Failed database calls. ellasmsc_database_storage_bytes Gauge Size of the database on disk, by file: main, wal. go_* Gauge, Counter, Summary Go runtime: goroutines, heap, garbage-collection pauses. process_* Gauge, Counter Process: memory, CPU, open file descriptors, start time.

docs.title: SMPP
docs.text:
Ella SMSC is an SMPP 3.4 SMSC for External Short Message Entities (ESMEs), such as OTA platforms. An ESME submits short messages to phones with submit_sm, and receives delivery receipts and SIM answers as deliver_sm.

The listener runs when the configuration file has an smpp block. ESME accounts are managed with the ESMEs API or the SMPP page of the UI.

"§" without a TS number refers to SMPP v3.4, Issue 1.2. Convention marks a behaviour that SMPP 3.4 does not define. All conventions are listed under Conventions.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: Item Value Transport TCP (§2.4), on smpp.port, default 2775. TLS With smpp.tls: TLS 1.2 or later, from the first octet. A listener is either plain or TLS. Convention. Client address The address of the TCP connection. The PROXY protocol is not supported. interface_version 0x34. SMSC system_id EllaSMSC, in bind responses. command_length 16 to 69,632 octets (68 KiB). Convention: SMPP 3.4 sets no maximum (§3.2.1). sequence_number 0x00000001 to 0x7FFFFFFF (§5.1.4).

docs.title: Supported
docs.text: PDU Direction Session state Handling bind_transmitter, bind_receiver, bind_transceiver ESME → SMSC OPEN See Binds. submit_sm ESME → SMSC BOUND_TX, BOUND_TRX One short message. See submit_sm. deliver_sm SMSC → ESME BOUND_RX, BOUND_TRX Delivery receipts and SIM answers. See Notifications. enquire_link Both Bound Answered at once (§4.11). unbind Both Bound See Session end. generic_nack Both Any Sent for a PDU that cannot be handled (§4.3). Received in answer to a deliver_sm: a temporary failure.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
PDU received Response Session command_length under 16 or over 68 KiB generic_nack ESME_RINVCMDLEN Closed sequence_number of 0 or over 0x7FFFFFFF generic_nack ESME_RUNKNOWNERR, sequence_number 0 Stays up query_sm, replace_sm, cancel_sm, submit_multi, data_sm, outbind, deliver_sm, an undefined or reserved command_id generic_nack ESME_RINVCMDID Stays up alert_notification None: discarded (§4.12) Stays up A bind in a bound state Its response with ESME_RALYBND Stays up Another request in a state that does not allow it (§2.3, Table 2-1) Its response with ESME_RINVBNDSTS Stays up A body on a PDU that has none, or a body shorter than its mandatory parameters generic_nack ESME_RINVCMDLEN Stays up A C-Octet String over its maximum length Its response with ESME_RINVPARLEN Stays up Optional parameters that do not decode as TLVs Its response with ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM Stays up A response that matches no request None: discarded Stays up

Unknown TLVs, and known TLVs not expected for the PDU, are ignored (§3.3). Responses may go out of order: they match their requests by sequence_number (§2.5.2).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The SMSC checks a bind in this order:

  1. At most 20 binds per minute from the client address: per IPv4 address, or per IPv6 /64.
  2. interface_version is 0x34 or later.
  3. At most 100 wrong passwords per hour for the system_id, from inside its allowed networks. A successful bind resets the count. Wrong passwords from outside the allowed networks, and binds with an unknown system_id, are counted apart, with the same limit, and never lock out the account.
  4. system_id and password match an ESME account. A check against an unknown system_id takes as long as one against a known system_id.
  5. The client address is in the account's allowed_networks. An empty list allows no address.

  6. The role of the account's user allows the bind type:

    Bind Permissions Roles Transmitter Send messages Admin, Network Manager, Submitter Receiver Read messages and their content Admin, Network Manager, Submitter Transceiver Both Admin, Network Manager, Submitter

    See Roles.

  7. Fewer than 4 sessions of the account are bound.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Outcome command_status Body Accepted ESME_ROK system_id EllaSMSC, and sc_interface_version 0x34 (§5.3.2.25). Refused, any check ESME_RBINDFAIL, never ESME_RINVSYSID or ESME_RINVPASWD None. bind_transceiver_resp: system_id EllaSMSC (Table 4-6).

The log gives the reason of a refused bind, with the system_id and the client address, at level info.

docs.title: Bind fields
docs.text: Field Handling system_id Up to 15 characters (§4.1.1). password Up to 8 characters (§4.1.1). interface_version See Checks. system_type, addr_ton, addr_npi, address_range Ignored.

docs.title: Account changes
docs.text: Updating or deleting an ESME, or changing the role of or deleting its user, closes its sessions.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Item Value Sessions per ESME 4, of any bind types. ESME accounts 50. Inbound window 64 requests handled at once per session. One more is answered ESME_RTHROTTLED. §2.5.2 recommends at most 10 outstanding. Outbound window 10 deliver_sm without a response per session (§2.6.2).

docs.title: Timers
docs.text:
The timers are fixed (§7.2).

Timer Value Action session_init_timer 30 s A connection that has not bound is closed. enquire_link_timer 30 s without a PDU received The SMSC sends enquire_link, and closes the session without a response within the response_timer. inactivity_timer 90 s without a PDU received The session is closed. response_timer 30 s A deliver_sm without a response is a temporary failure.

docs.title: Session end
docs.text: Event Handling unbind from the ESME The SMSC finishes the submit_sm in progress, answers unbind_resp, waits up to 2 s for the ESME to close the connection, then closes it (§2.2, §4.2). A submit_sm received meanwhile is answered ESME_RINVBNDSTS. SMSC shutdown The SMSC sends unbind to each session, waits up to 5 s for unbind_resp, then closes.

docs.title: submit_sm
docs.text:
One submit_sm stores exactly one SMS-SUBMIT: one message of the Messages API, owned by the ESME's user, delivered as a message from the API.

submit_sm_resp carries message_id: the id of the message in the Messages API, in decimal. The SMSC answers once the message is stored.

docs.title: Addressing
docs.text:
The destination is a phone, routed through the HSS (§5.2.5, §5.2.6, §5.2.9; TS 23.040 §9.1.2.5):

dest_addr_ton dest_addr_npi destination_addr 1, international 0 or 1 The international number. 0, unknown, or 2, national 0 or 1 Converted to international with the operator's numbering plan. Error command_status Another dest_addr_ton ESME_RINVDSTTON Another dest_addr_npi ESME_RINVDSTNPI Not 1 to 20 digits, or not 1 to 15 digits without a leading 0 once international ESME_RINVDSTADR

The source is shown to the recipient as the sender (§5.2.8):

source_addr_ton source_addr_npi source_addr Sent to the phone as 1, international 0 or 1 1 to 15 digits, no leading 0 TON 1, NPI 1 5, alphanumeric Any 1 to 11 letters and digits, single spaces between words, not all digits TON 5 0, 2, 3, 4 or 6 0, 1, 3, 4, 8, 9 or 10 1 to 20 digits The TON and NPI given Error command_status Empty source_addr ESME_RINVSRCADR. The SMSC has no default source. A reserved source_addr_ton ESME_RINVSRCTON Another source_addr_npi ESME_RINVSRCNPI. The NPIs accepted have the same value and meaning in §5.2.6 and TS 23.040 §9.1.2.5. Another source_addr ESME_RINVSRCADR

docs.title: data_coding
docs.text:
data_coding (§5.2.19) is mapped to a TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4):

data_coding SMPP 3.4 meaning TP-DCS and user data 0x00 SMSC default alphabet TP-DCS 0x00. The octets are GSM 7-bit default alphabet septets, one per octet, 0x1B for the extension table. An octet over 0x7F: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. Convention. 0x01 IA5 (ASCII) Converted to GSM 7-bit, TP-DCS 0x00, or to UCS2, TP-DCS 0x08, when a character has no GSM 7-bit equivalent. An octet over 0x7F: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0x02 Octet unspecified TP-DCS 0x04, 8-bit. 0x03 Latin-1 Converted to GSM 7-bit, TP-DCS 0x00, or to UCS2, TP-DCS 0x08, when a character has no GSM 7-bit equivalent. 0x04 Octet unspecified TP-DCS 0x04, 8-bit. 0x08 UCS2 TP-DCS 0x08, octets copied. An odd number of octets: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0xF0 to 0xF7 GSM message class control Copied. 0xC0 to 0xDF GSM message waiting indication ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0x05 to 0x07, 0x09 to 0xBF, 0xE0 to 0xEF, 0xF8 to 0xFF Other character sets, or reserved ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. SMPP 3.4 has no status for an invalid data_coding.

With a GSM 7-bit TP-DCS, the SMSC packs the septets after the user data header, with fill bits (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24).

dest_addr_subunit (§5.3.2.1, §5.2.19 note e) sets the message class bits of TP-DCS:

dest_addr_subunit Class 0, 5 to 255 Unchanged. 1, MS display Class 0 2, mobile equipment Class 1 3, smart card Class 2 4, external unit Class 3

A different class already in data_coding, or a TP-DCS without class bits: ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL.

(U)SIM data download. With protocol_id 0x7F, data_coding 0x02 or 0x04 and no dest_addr_subunit, TP-DCS is 0xF6, 8-bit data, class 2. Convention: TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9 requires class 2 for (U)SIM data download.

docs.title: esm_class
docs.text: Bits (§5.2.12) Value Handling 1-0, messaging mode 00 default, 11 store and forward Store and forward. 1-0 01 datagram, 10 transaction ESME_RINVESMCLASS 5-2, message type 0010, 0100, ESME acknowledgements ESME_RINVESMCLASS 5-2 Other Normal message (§3.3). 6, UDHI 1 TP-UDHI = 1. The user data starts with the user data header, its length octet included. A header longer than the user data: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 7, reply path 1 ESME_RINVESMCLASS

docs.title: protocol_id
docs.text:
Copied to TP-PID (§5.2.13; TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9):

protocol_id Handling 0x20 to 0x3E, telematic interworking ESME_RSUBMITFAIL 0x41 to 0x47, replace short message types 1 to 7 Replaces the pending message of the same type, from the same source, submitted by the same ESME. A message from a phone, the API or another ESME is never replaced. Convention. 0x48, device triggering Needs an application port addressing information element, else ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0x7C, 0x7F Need message class 2 after the data_coding mapping, else ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. Other Copied.

docs.title: registered_delivery
docs.text:
registered_delivery (§5.2.17) asks for notifications to the ESME. It does not set TP-Status-Report-Request.

Bits Value Handling 1-0 00 No receipt. 1-0 01 A receipt on the final status. 1-0 10 A receipt on failure only: failed, expired or replaced. 1-0 11 Reserved: no receipt (§3.3). 3-2 10 or 11, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement The SIM answer. 3-2 01, SME Delivery Acknowledgement Accepted, not honoured. 4 1, intermediate notification Accepted, not honoured.

docs.title: Validity and scheduling
docs.text:
Field Handling validity_period Empty: the default validity of the delivery settings. Absolute or relative (§7.1.1): the end of the validity period. In the past or malformed: ESME_RINVEXPIRY. The SMS-DELIVER carries no validity period. schedule_delivery_time Not empty: ESME_RINVSCHED.

A two-digit year is read within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year. Convention.

docs.title: User data and optional parameters
docs.text: Field Handling short_message (§5.2.22), message_payload (§5.3.2.32) One or the other. Both: ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD. sm_length Must match short_message. 255, or a mismatch: ESME_RINVMSGLEN. User data Must fit one TPDU once mapped: 140 octets, or 160 septets, the user data header included. Else ESME_RINVMSGLEN. The SMSC does not split user data. sar_msg_ref_num, sar_total_segments, sar_segment_seqnum All three: a concatenation information element, 0x00 with a reference up to 255, else 0x08 (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24.1, §9.2.3.24.8). Not all three: ignored. A total of 0, or a sequence number of 0 or over the total: ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL. source_port, destination_port A 16-bit application port addressing information element, 0x05 (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24.4). A missing one of the two is port 0. Convention. sar_* or ports with UDHI set ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD (§5.2.12). user_message_reference Echoed in the receipt and the SIM answer. sm_default_msg_id 1 to 254: ESME_RINVDFTMSGID. The SMSC has no canned messages. replace_if_present_flag 1: ESME_RINVSUBREP. Other values: taken as 0. service_type, priority_flag, other optional parameters Ignored.

docs.title: Order of submit_sm_resp and deliver_sm
docs.text: The message is handed to delivery once submit_sm_resp is written. A notification on the message can still reach the ESME before its submit_sm_resp when another message to the same recipient is being delivered.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
When a message from an ESME reaches its final status, the SMSC queues the SIM answer, then the receipt, that the submit_sm asked for, and sends them as deliver_sm.

Item Handling Session A receiver or transceiver session of the ESME that submitted the message, the one with the fewest deliver_sm in flight. Convention. No receiving session Notifications wait until the ESME binds as receiver or transceiver. They survive a restart. Order Notifications on one message go one at a time: the receipt waits until the SIM answer is acknowledged, rejected or expired. deliver_sm_resp ESME_ROK Acknowledged. deliver_sm_resp ESME_RX_P_APPN or ESME_RX_R_APPN Rejected. Not sent again. ESME_RX_T_APPN, another status, generic_nack, or no response within the response_timer Sent again after 1 minute, then doubling, at most every hour. Session closed or unbinding during the send Sent again at once on another receiving session, or on the next bind. Expiry The default validity of the delivery settings, from the message's final status. An expired notification is not sent. ESME deleted Its notifications are dropped.

Notifications are delivered at least once. The SIM answer and the receipt of a message share its receipted_message_id, and differ by the message type of esm_class.

docs.title: Delivery receipts
docs.text:
A receipt is an SMSC Delivery Receipt (§2.11, §4.6.1, Appendix B):

Field Value source_addr_ton, source_addr_npi, source_addr The destination of the message, as submitted. dest_addr_ton, dest_addr_npi, destination_addr The source of the message, as submitted. esm_class 0x04, SMSC Delivery Receipt. protocol_id, priority_flag, registered_delivery 0. data_coding 0x01, IA5. Convention. short_message The receipt text. receipted_message_id (0x001E) The message_id. message_state (0x0427) See the table below. user_message_reference (0x0204) That of the submit_sm, when present.

The text follows the example format of Appendix B:

id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:
Field Value id The message_id, not padded. sub 001. dlvrd 001 for a delivered message, else 000. submit date When the SMSC received the message, YYMMDDhhmm, UTC. done date When the message reached its final status, YYMMDDhhmm, UTC. For a replaced message, when it was replaced. Convention. stat, err See the table below. text Empty. Message status stat message_state (§5.2.28) err delivered DELIVRD 2 000 expired EXPIRED 3 070, TP-Status 0x46 replaced DELETED 4 002, TP-Status 0x02 failed UNDELIV 5 The TP-Status of the failure, such as 066, TP-Status 0x42

err is the TP-Status (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15), in decimal. Convention. network_error_code is not sent.

docs.title: SIM answers
docs.text:
The SIM answer is the TP-User-Data of the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT of the last delivery attempt (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a), from the RP-ACK, or from the RP-ERROR of an SM delivery failure. For a (U)SIM data download message, it is the SIM's Response Packet (TS 31.115 §4.4; TS 31.111 §7.1.1.1).

It is sent when registered_delivery bits 3-2 are 10 or 11, for any protocol_id, as an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement (§2.11). Convention.

No SIM answer is sent for a replaced message, or when the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has no TP-User-Data.

Field Value Addresses As in a receipt. esm_class message type 0100, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement. Convention. esm_class UDHI 1 when the report has TP-UDHI, or when the message's TP-PID is 0x7F and the user data starts with a valid user data header (TS 31.115 §4.1). Else 0. esm_class, typical 0x50 protocol_id The report's TP-PID, else the message's. data_coding See the table below. short_message The TP-User-Data, its user data header included, such as 027100…. receipted_message_id The message_id. Convention: §5.3.2.12 defines it for receipts. message_state Absent. user_message_reference That of the submit_sm, when present. Report TP-DCS data_coding short_message GSM 7-bit, or no TP-DCS (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.27) 0x00 Septets, one per octet. UCS2 0x08 The octets. 8-bit That of the submit_sm when it is 0x02, 0x04 or 0xF4 to 0xF7, else 0x04 The octets.

A SIM that rejects a (U)SIM data download message answers with an RP-ERROR whose TP-Failure-Cause is 0xD5, (U)SIM data download error. The message fails at once with TP-Status 0x42: the ESME gets the SIM answer, then the receipt stat:UNDELIV err:066.

docs.title: command_status values
docs.text:
Values the SMSC sends (§5.1.3):

command_status Value Sent in When ESME_ROK 0x00000000 Any response Success. ESME_RINVMSGLEN 0x00000001 submit_sm_resp sm_length, or user data longer than one TPDU. ESME_RINVCMDLEN 0x00000002 generic_nack command_length, or a body of the wrong length. ESME_RINVCMDID 0x00000003 generic_nack Unsupported or undefined command_id. ESME_RINVBNDSTS 0x00000004 Response A request that the session state does not allow. ESME_RALYBND 0x00000005 Bind response A bind in a bound state. ESME_RSYSERR 0x00000008 submit_sm_resp The message could not be stored or encoded. ESME_RINVSRCADR 0x0000000A submit_sm_resp source_addr. ESME_RINVDSTADR 0x0000000B submit_sm_resp destination_addr. ESME_RBINDFAIL 0x0000000D Bind response Any refused bind. ESME_RINVSUBREP 0x00000042 submit_sm_resp replace_if_present_flag 1. ESME_RINVESMCLASS 0x00000043 submit_sm_resp esm_class. ESME_RSUBMITFAIL 0x00000045 submit_sm_resp data_coding, protocol_id, the user data header, or GSM 7-bit, IA5 or UCS2 user data. ESME_RINVSRCTON 0x00000048 submit_sm_resp source_addr_ton. ESME_RINVSRCNPI 0x00000049 submit_sm_resp source_addr_npi. ESME_RINVDSTTON 0x00000050 submit_sm_resp dest_addr_ton. ESME_RINVDSTNPI 0x00000051 submit_sm_resp dest_addr_npi. ESME_RTHROTTLED 0x00000058 submit_sm_resp Inbound window full. ESME_RINVSCHED 0x00000061 submit_sm_resp schedule_delivery_time. ESME_RINVEXPIRY 0x00000062 submit_sm_resp validity_period. ESME_RINVDFTMSGID 0x00000063 submit_sm_resp sm_default_msg_id. ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM 0x000000C0 Response Optional parameters that do not decode. ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD 0x000000C1 submit_sm_resp short_message with message_payload; sar_* or ports with UDHI. ESME_RINVPARLEN 0x000000C2 Response A field over its maximum length, or a TLV of the wrong length. ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL 0x000000C4 submit_sm_resp sar_* values; dest_addr_subunit against data_coding; a TLV that should be a C-Octet String and is not. ESME_RUNKNOWNERR 0x000000FF generic_nack Invalid sequence_number.

An error response has no body (§4.1.2, §4.1.4, §4.4.2), except bind_transceiver_resp, which carries system_id (Table 4-6). The SMSC logs the reason of a refused submit_sm at level debug, with the system_id.

Values the SMSC acts on in deliver_sm_resp: see Notifications.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Behaviours that SMPP 3.4 does not define:

Behaviour Where TLS from the first octet. Transport A maximum command_length of 68 KiB. Transport data_coding 0x00 is the GSM 7-bit default alphabet, unpacked. data_coding data_coding 0x02 or 0x04 with protocol_id 0x7F becomes TP-DCS 0xF6, class 2. data_coding A replace type protocol_id replaces only messages of the same ESME. protocol_id A two-digit year is within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year. Validity and scheduling A missing source_port or destination_port is port 0. User data and optional parameters Notifications go to a receiving session of the ESME that submitted the message. Notifications Receipts use data_coding 0x01. Delivery receipts A replaced message's receipt is DELETED, with done date the replacement time. Delivery receipts Receipt err is the TP-Status in decimal. Delivery receipts The SIM's answer is an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement, with receipted_message_id. SIM answers

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• SMPP 3.3 and earlier, and SMPP 5.0.
  • query_sm, replace_sm, cancel_sm, submit_multi, data_sm, alert_notification and outbind.
  • Messages from phones to ESMEs, such as a Response Packet that the SIM sends in an SMS-SUBMIT (TS 31.115 §4.2).
  • Splitting user data longer than one TPDU.
  • Scheduled delivery, the datagram and transaction modes, SME delivery acknowledgements and intermediate notifications.
  • The PROXY protocol.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Requests send a token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is either:

  • an access token, from log in or refresh the access token, valid for 15 minutes;
  • an API token, which starts with ellasmsc_.

These paths take no token: GET /api/v1/livez, GET /api/v1/readyz, GET /api/v1/status, GET /api/v1/metrics, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml, POST /api/v1/init, and POST /api/v1/auth/login, /refresh and /logout.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role role_id Allows Admin 1 Everything. Read Only 2 Reading messages without their content, Diameter, operator, delivery and retention settings, and ESMEs. Network Manager 3 Read Only, plus reading message content, sending messages, updating operator, delivery and retention settings, and managing Diameter peers. Submitter 4 Sending messages, and reading the messages it sent, their content included.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users or ESMEs.

Only an Admin manages ESMEs. An ESME binds over SMPP with the role of its user.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Ella SMSC's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a result:

{
    "result": "Result content"
}

A failed response carries an error:

{
    "error": "Error message"
}

GET /api/v1/livez and GET /api/v1/readyz answer 204 with no body when they succeed. GET /api/v1/metrics returns text in the Prometheus exposition format, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

Times are RFC 3339, in UTC.

docs.title: OpenAPI Specification
docs.text:
The full API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella SMSC instance:

GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
• 200 - Success.
  • 201 - Created.
  • 204 - No content.
  • 400 - Bad request.
  • 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
  • 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
  • 404 - Not found.
  • 405 - Method not allowed.
  • 409 - Conflict.
  • 429 - Too many requests. Retry-After is the seconds to wait.
  • 500 - Internal server error.
  • 503 - Not ready. See Check readiness.

docs.title: Log In
docs.text:
This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, smsc_session, or __Host-smsc_session over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/login

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address, in any case. password string Yes Password.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Wrong email or password. 429 More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Refresh the Access Token
docs.text:
This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/refresh

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Log Out
docs.text:
This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/logout

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 204 Logged out, or no session.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text: The delivery settings set how long the SMSC attempts delivery of a message, and when it retries a failed delivery. The retention sets how long it keeps a message afterwards.

docs.title: Get the Delivery Settings
docs.text:
This path returns the delivery settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/delivery

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description default_validity_seconds int How long delivery of a message without its own validity period is attempted, in seconds. The same applies to status reports. retry_intervals_seconds array Wait before each retry, in seconds. The last interval repeats. Empty: a failed delivery is not retried.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 604800,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300, 900, 3600]
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Delivery Settings
docs.text:
This path replaces the delivery settings. The new validity applies to the messages received afterwards; the new intervals, to the next retries.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/delivery

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description default_validity_seconds int Yes 1 to 315360000 (10 years). retry_intervals_seconds array Yes Each at least 1.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
    "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
    }
}

docs.title: Diameter
docs.text: Configured peers are the Diameter agents that the SMSC connects to, and their routes. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Network Manager or Admin.

docs.title: Get the Diameter Status
docs.text:
This path returns the Diameter identity of the SMSC, its peers, and its routes.

Method Path GET /api/v1/diameter

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description host string Origin-Host of the SMSC. realm string Origin-Realm of the SMSC. peers array Connected and configured peers. peers[].id int ID of a configured peer. peers[].configured boolean Whether the peer is configured. peers[].host string Origin-Host of the peer. peers[].realm string Origin-Realm of the peer. peers[].address string Remote address of the connection. peers[].state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. peers[].applications array Applications the peer supports: s6c, sgd. peers[].since string Time of the last state change. peers[].error string Last connection error of a configured peer. routes array The s6c route to the HSS, then the routes of the configured peers, default routes last. routes[].realm string Destination-Realm. Empty for a default route. routes[].default boolean Whether the route is a default route. routes[].application string s6c or sgd. routes[].peers array Hosts of the open peers of the route.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "host": "smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "peers": [
            {
                "configured": false,
                "host": "core.example.org",
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "address": "127.0.0.1",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.330Z"
            },
            {
                "id": 1,
                "configured": true,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                "address": "192.0.2.10",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
            }
        ],
        "routes": [
            {
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "default": false,
                "application": "s6c",
                "peers": ["core.example.org"]
            },
            {
                "realm": "",
                "default": true,
                "application": "sgd",
                "peers": ["dea1.ipx.example.net"]
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: List Peers
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/diameter/peers

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
                "port": 3868,
                "routes": [
                    { "default": true, "application": "sgd", "priority": 0 }
                ],
                "status": {
                    "state": "open",
                    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                    "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                    "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Create a Peer
docs.text: Method Path POST /api/v1/diameter/peers

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description host string No Origin-Host the peer must give. Empty accepts any. addresses array Yes IP addresses of the peer. A peer with a host must connect from one of them. port int No Default 3868. routes array No Routes of the peer. routes[].realm string Unless default Destination-Realm, e.g. epc.mnc002.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org. routes[].default boolean No Default route: every realm without another route, except the SMSC's own. sgd only, without realm. routes[].application string Yes sgd or s6c. An s6c route takes the SMSC's own realm. routes[].priority int No Lowest first; equal priorities share the load. Default 0.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
    "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
    "routes": [
        { "default": true, "application": "sgd" },
        { "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org", "application": "s6c" }
    ]
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 The peer, with its id. 400 Invalid peer. 409 host is another peer's or the SMSC's, or two peers without a host share an address.

docs.title: Get a Peer
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
The fields of the request body, plus:

Field Type Description id int ID of the peer. status object Connection to the peer. Absent until the SMSC applies the peer, and from the responses to create and update. status.state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. status.host string Origin-Host the peer gave. status.realm string Origin-Realm the peer gave. status.since string Time of the last state change. status.error string Last connection error.

docs.title: Update a Peer
docs.text:
The request body is that of Create a Peer. A change of host, addresses or port reconnects.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}

docs.title: Delete a Peer
docs.text: Method Path DELETE /api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}

docs.title: ESMEs
docs.text:
An ESME account is what an External Short Message Entity, such as an OTA platform, binds to the SMPP listener with, with at most 4 sessions at once. It acts as its user: the messages it submits are the user's, and the user's role decides which binds it may make. See Binds.

Reading ESMEs requires Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: List ESMEs
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/esmes

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description system_id string The system_id the ESME binds with. user string Email of the user the ESME acts as. allowed_networks array IP prefixes the ESME may bind from. created_at string Time the ESME was created. sessions array Bound sessions, oldest first. sessions[].bind_type string transmitter, receiver or transceiver. sessions[].remote_address string Address and port of the client. sessions[].bound_at string Time of the bind.

The password is never returned.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "system_id": "ota",
                "user": "ota@example.com",
                "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
                "sessions": [
                    {
                        "bind_type": "transceiver",
                        "remote_address": "10.1.0.5:40312",
                        "bound_at": "2026-10-27T18:41:55.906Z"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Create an ESME
docs.text:
At most 50 ESMEs. Without a password, the SMSC generates one of 8 letters and digits, and returns it as password in this response only.

Method Path POST /api/v1/esmes

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description system_id string Yes 1 to 15 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1). user string Yes Email of an existing user, the user the ESME acts as. password string No 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1). Default: generated. allowed_networks array No IP prefixes, such as 10.1.0.0/24 or 2001:db8::/64, at most 50. Default: none, which allows no address.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "system_id": "ota",
    "user": "ota@example.com",
    "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "system_id": "ota",
        "user": "ota@example.com",
        "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
        "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
        "sessions": [],
        "password": "q7Rk2LxW"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 The ESME, with the generated password when none was given. 400 Invalid field, no user with the email, or 50 ESMEs exist. 409 An ESME has the system_id.

docs.title: Get an ESME
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/esmes/{system_id}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description system_id string The system_id of the ESME, URL-encoded.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No ESME has this system_id.

docs.title: Update an ESME
docs.text:
This path replaces the allowed networks of an ESME, and its password when one is given, and closes its sessions, which bind again under the new settings. The system_id and the user cannot be changed.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/esmes/{system_id}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description password string No 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters. Without it, the password stays. allowed_networks array Yes As in Create an ESME.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 The ESME. 400 Invalid field. 404 No ESME has this system_id.

docs.title: Delete an ESME
docs.text:
This path deletes an ESME, closes its sessions, and drops the receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to it. Its messages stay, as its user's. Deleting the user deletes its ESMEs.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/esmes/{system_id}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "ESME deleted successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Initialize Ella SMSC
docs.text:
This path creates the first user, an Admin, and logs it in.

Method Path POST /api/v1/init

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address. password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 403 A user exists. 429 Too many attempts from the client address.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "correct horse"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "System initialized successfully",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
A message is a short message the SMSC received, from a phone, from the API, or from an ESME over SMPP, with its delivery status and the status reports the SMSC returned to the phone that sent it. A text longer than one short message is split into parts, one message each.

Responses carry no content. Get the content of a message returns it, and logs an audit event.

docs.title: Create a Message
docs.text:
This path submits a text message, or a binary message, to a phone. It returns one message per part.

Method Path POST /api/v1/messages

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description from string Yes Shown to the recipient as the sender. An E.164 number with +, or a name of 1 to 11 ASCII letters and digits, with single spaces between words, that is not all digits, such as EllaSMSC. A value without + is a name, delivered as given. to string Yes E.164 number with + of the recipient. text string One of text and binary Not empty. GSM-7 if every character is in the GSM 7-bit default alphabet or its extension table, else UCS-2. Up to 255 parts. binary object One of text and binary TPDU parameters of one short message, delivered unchanged. binary.protocol_identifier int No TP-PID (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9), 0 to 255. Default 0. Not 32 to 62, telematic interworking. 65 to 71, replace types 1 to 7, replace the pending message of the same type from the same from, submitted by the same user; never a message from a phone or an ESME. 72, device triggering, needs an application port addressing information element in user_data_header. binary.data_coding_scheme int Yes TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4), 0 to 255. Not a GSM 7-bit, UCS2 or reserved coding. Message class 2 when protocol_identifier is 124, ANSI-136 R-DATA, or 127, (U)SIM data download. binary.user_data_header string No TP-UDH (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24) in hexadecimal, its length octet included. binary.user_data string Yes TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal. May be empty. At most 140 octets with user_data_header. Not split into parts. validity_seconds int No How long delivery is attempted, 1 to 315360000 (10 years). Default: the default validity of the delivery settings.

A message from the API never asks for status reports.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 A field is missing or invalid, both or neither of text and binary, the text needs more than 255 parts, or the binary user data is over 140 octets.

docs.title: Sample Request (Binary)
docs.text:
{
    "from": "+15550001000",
    "to": "+15551230002",
    "binary": {
        "protocol_identifier": 127,
        "data_coding_scheme": 246,
        "user_data_header": "027000",
        "user_data": "0011223344"
    }
}

docs.title: List Messages
docs.text:
This path returns the list of messages, most recent first. For a Submitter, only the messages it sent.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description to query str 1 to 15 digits, after an optional + Recipient: the numbers that contain these digits. +1555123 and 1555123 match +15551230002, and so does 0002. from query str 1 to 15 digits, after an optional +, or a name as in Create a Message Sender: the numbers that contain these digits, or the name, in any case. status query str pending, delivered, failed, expired, replaced Status. start query str RFC 3339 time Created at or after. end query str RFC 3339 time, not before start Created before. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id int Message identifier. from string Sender: the MSISDN of the phone, an E.164 number with +, the from of the API request, or the source_addr of the submit_sm, with + when international. to string Recipient, an E.164 number with +. encoding string gsm7, ucs2 or binary. concatenation object Present for a part of a longer message. concatenation.reference int Reference shared by the parts of the message. concatenation.part int Number of this part, from 1. concatenation.total int Number of parts. status string pending; delivered; failed; expired, when its validity period ended before its delivery; or replaced, by a later message from the same sender, of the same replace type, before its delivery. created_at string Time the SMSC received the message. updated_at string Time of the last change. expires_at string End of the validity period. next_attempt_at string Time of the next delivery attempt. Present while pending. status_report object Status reports on the message. status_report.requested boolean Whether the phone that sent the message asked for status reports. status_report.reports array Status reports the SMSC returned to that phone, oldest first. status_report.reports[].id int Status report identifier. status_report.reports[].tp_status int TP-Status the report gives (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15). status_report.reports[].tp_status_name string Meaning of tp_status, e.g. received, replaced, no_response, validity_period_expired. status_report.reports[].status string Delivery of the report to the phone: pending, delivered, failed or expired. status_report.reports[].created_at string Time the SMSC made the report. status_report.reports[].updated_at string Time of the last change. status_report.reports[].expires_at string End of the report's validity period. status_report.reports[].next_attempt_at string Time of the next delivery attempt of the report. Present while pending. submitted_by string Email of the user that sent the message over the API, or of the user of the ESME that sent it over SMPP. Absent for a message from a phone. system_id string system_id of the ESME that sent the message over SMPP. Absent for other messages, and once the ESME is deleted.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/content

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description id int Message identifier.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description text string Text of the part. Absent for a binary message. binary object TPDU parameters of a binary message. binary.protocol_identifier int TP-PID. binary.data_coding_scheme int TP-DCS. binary.user_data_header string TP-UDH in hexadecimal, its length octet included. Absent when there are none. deliver_reports[].attempt_id int Delivery attempt of the report: in the RP-ACK when its outcome is success, else in the RP-ERROR. deliver_reports[].tpdu string The report in hexadecimal. The other deliver_reports[] fields are absent when it does not decode. deliver_reports[].protocol_identifier int TP-PID, when present. deliver_reports[].data_coding_scheme int TP-DCS, when present. deliver_reports[].user_data_header string TP-UDH in hexadecimal, when present. deliver_reports[].user_data string TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal, when present.
