docs.title: List Delivery Attempts
docs.text:
This path returns the routing and delivery attempts of a message, oldest first. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/attempts

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description id int Message identifier.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description id int Attempt identifier. started_at string Start of the attempt. completed_at string End of the attempt. step string routing: a routing lookup at the HSS, over S6c. delivery: a delivery to a serving node, over SGd. node string Host of the HSS that answered the routing lookup, or of the serving node. node_type string Type of the serving node: mme, sgsn, ip_sm_gw, smsf_3gpp or smsf_non_3gpp. outcome string success; no_hss, no HSS connected; unreachable, the serving node not connected; timeout, no answer in time; the error the node gave: user_unknown, absent_user, user_busy_for_mt_sms, facility_not_supported, illegal_user, illegal_equipment, sm_delivery_failure, service_not_subscribed, service_barred, mwd_list_full; diameter_error, another error answer; or error. result_code int Result-Code or Experimental-Result-Code of the answer. vendor_id int Vendor-Id of an Experimental-Result-Code. failure_cause string SM-Delivery-Failure-Cause of an sm_delivery_failure. tp_failure_cause string TP-Failure-Cause the phone gave. absent_user_diagnostics object Why the phone is unreachable, by node: mme, msc, sgsn, ip_sm_gw, smsf_3gpp, smsf_non_3gpp.

A value the SMSC did not observe is absent.

docs.title: Get Metrics
docs.text:
This path returns the metrics of the SMSC in the Prometheus exposition format, negotiated from the request's Accept header. See Observability for the list.

Method Path GET /api/v1/metrics

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
# HELP ellasmsc_hss_peers Open Diameter peers in the operator's realm that serve S6c, which the SMSC asks to route messages. At 0, messages to phones wait.
# TYPE ellasmsc_hss_peers gauge
ellasmsc_hss_peers 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_pending Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type (message, status_report) and state: due (to be delivered now, or being delivered) or waiting (for a retry or for the phone to be reachable). Due messages that stay due mean the deliverer is falling behind.
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_pending gauge
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="message"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="status_report"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="message"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="status_report"} 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_received_total Short messages received, one per TPDU, by origin (mobile, api) and result (accepted, rejected, error).
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_received_total counter
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="accepted"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="accepted"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="rejected"} 0

docs.title: Operator
docs.text: The operator is the PLMN of the SMSC, from which its Diameter identity derives, its service centre address, and the numbering plan that converts the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers.

docs.title: Get the Operator
docs.text:
This path returns the operator settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcc string Mobile Country Code. mnc string Mobile Network Code. service_centre_address string E.164 number of the SMSC, which phones have as SMSC number. numbering object Conversion of the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers. numbering.country_code string Country code, added to the numbers phones send in national format. numbering.national_prefix string Prefix that phones dial before a national number, removed before the country code is added. Empty if none. numbering.international_prefix string Prefix that phones dial before an international number, removed. Empty if none.

docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description mcc string Yes 3 digits. mnc string Yes 2 or 3 digits. service_centre_address string Yes E.164 number with +, e.g. +15550000000. numbering object Yes numbering.country_code string Yes 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0. numbering.national_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. Differs from international_prefix unless empty. numbering.international_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits.

docs.text:
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011"
    }
}

{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {

docs.title: Pprof
docs.text: These paths serve the net/http/pprof API. They require Admin, and accept an API token.

docs.title: Profiling Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/pprof/ An HTML page listing the available profiles. GET /api/v1/pprof/allocs A sampling of all past memory allocations. GET /api/v1/pprof/cmdline The command line invocation of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutine Stack traces of all current goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak Stack traces of all leaked goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/heap A sampling of memory allocations of live objects. GET /api/v1/pprof/profile A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default. GET /api/v1/pprof/threadcreate Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. GET /api/v1/pprof/trace An execution trace, of 1 second by default. GET, POST /api/v1/pprof/symbol Function names of program counters.

docs.text: Parameter Paths Description seconds profile, trace Duration of the capture. seconds allocs, goroutine, heap Returns the difference of the profile over this duration. debug allocs, goroutine, heap, threadcreate 0: protobuf. 1: text. 2 (goroutine): stack traces in the format of a panic. gc heap 1: runs a garbage collection first.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: The retention sets how long the SMSC keeps a message once it has its final status: delivered, failed, expired or replaced. The SMSC then deletes it, with its status reports and delivery attempts, within the hour. It keeps a message until its status reports, too, have had their final status for that long.

docs.title: Get the Retention
docs.text:
This path returns the retention.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/retention

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description days int Days a message is kept once it has its final status. Default: 30.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "days": 30
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Retention
docs.text:
This path replaces the retention. It applies from the next deletion, within the hour.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/messages/retention

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description days int Yes At least 1.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "days": 7
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "days": 7
    }
}

docs.title: Check Liveness

This path answers while the process serves HTTP.

This path returns whether the SMSC can serve requests: its database answers, and it is not shutting down.

It answers 204 No Content when ready, and 503 Service Unavailable otherwise:

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add SMS to a private 5G network with Ella SMSC.

Tutorial Hardware Required Installation Method Duration Send Your First SMS An Ella Core 5G network, two phones Snap ~15 min

docs.title: Send Your First SMS
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add Ella SMSC to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and send an SMS between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 15 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need:

  • A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware) tutorial, with PLMN 00101.
  • Two phones attached to the network, with SIM cards whose SMSC number you can set.

docs.title: 1. Install Ella SMSC
docs.text:
On the host running Ella Core, install and start the Ella SMSC snap:

sudo snap install ella-smsc
sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: 2. Initialize Ella SMSC
docs.text:
Open your browser at http://<host-ip>:5010. The Initialize Ella SMSC page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click Create.

The Diameter page shows no connected peers yet.

docs.title: 3. Connect Ella Core
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to Operator and scroll to the SMS section.

Click Add Service Center and set:

  • Address: 127.0.0.1
  • Numbers: +15550000000
  • Diameter Identity: smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org

Click Add. The service center shows Connected.

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers, Ella Core shows open, with HSS set to yes.

docs.title: 4. Give the subscribers an MSISDN
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, for each of the two subscribers:

  • Go to Subscribers and open the subscriber.
  • In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to MSISDN.
  • Enter +15551230001 for the first subscriber and +15551230002 for the second, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Set the SMSC number on the SIM cards
docs.text: On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to +15550000000.

docs.title: 6. Send an SMS
docs.text:
From the first phone, send hello to +15551230002. The second phone receives it.

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Messages. The message shows delivered. Click it to see its routing and delivery attempts.

You have added SMS to your 5G network.
